1Warm-up · Work routines

Work from the office or from home?

Look at the pictures. Talk about your usual work routine and what can change this week.

Office routine

I usually work in the office.

Temporary change

This week I’m working from home.

Personal question
“Do you usually work from home or in an office?”

3BPresentation · The rules

When & howto use Present Simple and Present Continuous

Two tenses, two jobs. Read each card. Tap 🔊 to hear the example.

Present Simple
use it for things “in general”
We use it for…
habits & routinesI get up at seven.
factsWater boils at 100°C.
permanent thingsAnna drives to work every day.
Form
affirmative
I / you / we / theywork
he / she / itworks
negative
don’t / doesn’t+ verb
question
Do / Does+ subject + verb?
Signal words
Present Continuous
use it for things happening “now”
We use it for…
actions nowLook! It’s raining.
around nowI’m working from home this week.
temporary situationsAnna is taking the bus today.
Form
affirmative
Iam working
he / she / itis working
you / we / theyare working
negative
am not / isn’t / aren’t+ verb-ing
question
Am / Is / Are+ subject + verb-ing?
Signal words
Feel the difference
general · every day
"I work in an office."
Present Simple — my job, always true.
vs
now · temporary
"I'm working from home today."
Present Continuous — just today.
Spelling: verb + -ing
workworking
makemaking (drop e)
runrunning (double)
Most verbs: just add -ing.
Ends in -e? Drop the e: make → making.
Short verb with one vowelVowelsa · e · i · o · u + one consonantConsonantsb · c · d · f · g · h · j · k · l · m · n · p · q · r · s · t · v · w · x · y · z? Double the last letter: run → running, sit → sitting.
State verbs (not -ing)
Some verbs describe a state, not an action — we can't see another person doing them. We don't usually use -ing:
some of them: like · love · want · know · understand
✓ I know the answer.
✗ I am knowing the answer.
Check understanding (talk it through) ▸
  • ?"I'm reading a book." — Is this happening now, or every day?
  • ?"She drinks tea." — One time, or many times / usually?
  • ?Which tense goes with usually? Which goes with right now?
  • ?Can we say "I am wanting a coffee"? Why not?
"Now you know the two jobs of these tenses. Let's try them out — Anna and Mark are back!"
4Practice · Controlled≈ 25 min

Let's practise

A · Now or usually? Sort the time words
B · Choose the correct verb form
C · Spelling: make the -ing form
D · Negatives & questions
E · Picture flip · describe the people

Flip a card. Look at both pictures and talk about the person. Say what the person usually does and what is different now / today / this week. Try to use but and a negative sentence. For a longer answer, add because + a reason.

Example:
Anna usually drinks coffee at work, but today she isn’t drinking coffee (because she doesn’t have coffee).

F · Find & fix the mistake

Some sentences have a mistake, some are already correct. Click a word to cross it out (click again to bring it back); double-click a word to rewrite it. Fix each sentence, then show the answers.

G · State verbs · choose the right one
"You've got the grammar. Now the best part — let's talk about YOUR life: now and always."
